definition: A task requiring an AI agent to maintain coherent behavior, planning, and progress toward a goal over an extended sequence of steps or a long duration.
details: Long-horizon tasks are a key challenge for agentic AI systems, testing an agent's ability to maintain context, recover from errors, and avoid drifting off-track over many sequential actions.

explainer.lead: A long-horizon task requires an AI agent to maintain coherent behavior, planning and progress toward a goal over an extended sequence of steps or duration. It matters as a key challenge for agentic systems.

tiers.eli5: It is like a hiker on a multi-day trek who must keep the destination in mind, recover from wrong turns and not wander off course.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use these tasks to test whether agents hold context, recover from errors and avoid drifting off-track across many sequential actions. A pitfall is that small early errors compound over many steps, so progress checks and recovery mechanisms matter.
tiers.paperLevel: Evaluation centers on maintaining context, error recovery and goal progress across long action sequences; the core difficulty is compounding error and drift as the number of steps grows.

explainer.example: An agent refactoring a large codebase over hundreds of edits must track which files changed, revert a broken change, and keep the build passing.
